name: HT Media Ltd
title: HT Media Ltd - 532662 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HT Media Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly tripled to INR 90 crore, while a preferential issue drew shareholder pushback.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up about 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, and management credited yield improvement. Digital operating revenue fell about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore, as the portfolio was deliberately reset, and Radio was flat with negative INR 3 crore EBITDA after surrendering licences for non-viable stations. The board approved a preferential issue of equity to HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (not HMVL), priced at the SEBI formula (around INR 24-25 per share), which drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 111 crore a year earlier

segments.name: English Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue grew 12% YoY to INR 156 crore; circulation revenue grew 14% to INR 13 crore (about INR 1.5 crore absolute change, mostly pricing and mix).

segments.name: Hindi Print
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue rose YoY to INR 139 crore; circulation revenue flat.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Licences surrendered for certain non-viable stations.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% YoY; operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%) after deliberate portfolio reset; OTTplay decision taken around 31 March 2026 per management.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance; said it is 'very hopeful' of sustaining good numbers.

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of materials) at about USD 650-700 per tonne is the highest since COVID; management believes prices have peaked and will plateau before easing, but acknowledged no forward market exists.
Q2 newsprint expected slightly higher than Q1; Q1 Print margin of about 13% offered as a modelling baseline, with downside if dollar and newsprint rise further.
Preferential issue proceeds to retire 30-50% of the debt at HT Media and Digicontent; management says it is EPS-accretive and will improve interest coverage and credit rating.
Government ad and circulation rates were raised in November 2025 after seven years, so the price benefit continues for the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent Ltd (DCL), priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP); promoters subscribing on the same terms, up to their regulatory maximum; ongoing vote, with a shareholder voting against.
Radio footprint reduced by surrendering licences for non-viable stations.
Cost right-sizing: consolidated employee cost fell to INR 99 crore from INR 111 crore YoY.
HMVL cash (where most of the INR 922 crore net cash sits) to be deployed at HMVL board's discretion; no preferential issue at HMVL.
demand_pricing: Commercial print revenue held on volume with yield improvement as the main driver; government revenue grew on both volume and the November 2025 rate increase.
Management stated that a substantial part of the 15% revenue growth came from pricing, not volume.
Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers are already well priced and prior commodity-driven hikes were taken.
Circulation held steady market by market to protect copy share in English markets.
Other operating income at HMVL roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore (from about INR 10 crore), mainly job work and scrap sales.
Competitive environment described as likely to remain as is for circulation.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a preferential issue at about INR 24 per share, below book value of about INR 70, rather than a rights issue, given INR 922 crore net cash and a 15% dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all the net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and DCL are net debt companies. Preferential issue is faster (2-3 months), gives more certainty of raising the amount and avoids underwriter risk; pricing follows the SEBI formula with no premium. Proceeds will retire 30-50% of debt.

qa_highlights.question: Given the 15% dilution, the valuation and the moral/reputational issue, will the company withdraw the preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not agree to withdraw. It said price-to-book is below 0.5x, the promoters are subscribing on the same terms, and it is raising capital to retire debt and improve EPS. A shareholder said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt position consistent with earlier statements that the company was debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt has built up at HT Media over the last 3-4 years post-COVID (Print English and Radio); the combined net cash figure hides this, and the number is not new.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of HMVL's other income jump, and is it MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury gains from mutual funds (NAV-based) plus realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on investments. Treasury gains depend on yield curve movements and are not predictable.

qa_highlights.question: How will newsprint costs affect Print margins, and can prices be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint is 25-40% of the bill of materials. Management expects a plateau at current levels, so Q1 Print margin of about 13% can be used as a baseline if prices don't rise further; cover price increases are difficult.

qa_highlights.question: What drove ad revenue growth at Print, and what share is government revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly commercial yield improvement with volumes holding; government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Management did not disclose the government share and called it 'substantial' but smaller than commercial.

risks_watch: Newsprint at about USD 650-700 per tonne, the highest since COVID, with no forward market; Q2 newsprint guided slightly higher than Q1, and a weaker dollar adds to cost pressure on the 13% Print margin.

Preferential issue at HT Media and Digicontent: ~15% dilution at roughly INR 24-25 per share versus book value of about INR 70; shareholder voting is ongoing and at least one minority holder has voted against, so approval and final pricing remain open.
Debt at HT Media and DCL: management said 30-50% of debt will be retired from the issue proceeds; the net cash of INR 922 crore sits in HMVL, and the consolidated figure masks standalone net debt.
Other income at HMVL (treasury gains and profit on asset sales) is not predictable and depends on yield curve movements, so the Q1 profit level may not repeat.

Digital operating revenue down about 28% with EBITDA of negative INR 3 crore after the portfolio reset; Radio EBITDA negative INR 3 crore. Track whether these turn profitable next quarter and whether the Q1 earnings step-up holds once government rate benefits cycle out after two quarters.
key_quotes: So, a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing .
We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down.
Debt has been building in HT Media for the last 4-5 years post-COVID because of the Print English operations and Radio operations, etc.
Treasury gains is basically mutual funds and the NA V based process and not a MTM valuation-based process.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance, pricing and cost discipline, and on the preferential issue as a faster, certain route to cutting debt. Cautious and defensive on newsprint and dollar costs, and evasive on the debt history and share pricing, where answers repeatedly deflected to HMVL or the SEBI formula. No formal guidance was given.
